what: Perplexity with the KV cache stored as f32, int8 or int4 (groups of 32 values, one f32 scale per group), every token fed one at a time so each later token reads the stored history
command: cargo run --release --example kv_precision_ppl -- --model-path models/SmolLM-135M --tokens wikitext2_test.SmolLM-135M.u32 --window W --max-windows N
corpus: WikiText-2 test split, first N non-overlapping windows of the committed-format token file
known_gaps: Pythia-14M was measured separately and behaves very differently (docs/benchmarks/pythia-14m/data/kv_precision_ppl.json): int8 is not safe in general
4,096-token context not measured: SmolLM-135M and Pythia-14M are both trained for 2,048 positions, so a 4k run would test rope extrapolation, not the cache

windows are short (4 x 256 and 2 x 1,024 tokens) so the 256-token and 1,024-token perplexities are not comparable to each other or to the full-split figure; only the f32 versus int8 versus int4 difference inside one window setting is meaningful
no decode-speed measurement: reading the cache means decoding it for every token, the CPU path was not timed here
